items.title: Chazz Frichtel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 13, 2016
items.q: a piano player who was a guy that was Lou Rawls’ music director, Reg Powell

ctx.x: I’ve told Rick and Carmen that too. Because when I first moved up here I managed to get a gig with the both of them and Dolores Mancuso at the Beeches. And I just sat on my stool with my sax and I watched and listened to what they did. And I thought I knew a lot because I had gone to music school. But I didn’t know anything about playing gigs and filling what people’s expectations would be, or beyond. It was really an education for me.

Yeah. Playing here in the years that I did before I went to L.A. was just priceless. And I told Carmen yesterday, because Carmen pulled me in on a project in L.A. before I moved there. It was centered around a percussionist who played in the group Traffic. And his name was Rebop Kwaku Baah. He was a Nigerian prince percussionist. And Carmen had gotten a call from a piano player who was a guy that was Lou Rawls’ music director, Reg Powell, and a drummer, Jack Toker, lives in Seattle. And Reg was kind of putting…

first trip to L.A. And that was, whoa, eye opening on so many levels. As it turned out Rebop kind of disappeared. So to try and salvage, we had a few days left, two or three days left. Carmen had heard a couple of my original tunes and he says, “why don’t you play these for the guys?” So I played three songs of mine. And Reg said, “Let’s see if we can get some studio time at Conway Studios.” Which is still operating in L.A. We went in and cut three songs. And then we all went home and Reg and a lawyer friend of…
